problem: The flowchart disagrees with the text in Section 3. The 'yes' branch of 'effective uid is 0?' leads to 'owner bits apply', but root is not decided by the owner triplet; root skips the triplet check for read and write. The chart also has no node for 'effective uid equals the file's uid?', so a reader who owns a file but is not in the file's group is routed from 'in the file's group?' straight to 'other bits apply', which is wrong. Step 2 of the list in Section 3 is missing from the diagram.
fix: After 'effective uid is 0?': the 'yes' edge goes to a node 'allow read and write; execute needs an x bit'. The 'no' edge goes to a new node 'effective uid equals file uid?', whose 'yes' edge goes to 'owner bits apply' and whose 'no' edge goes to 'in the file's group?'. Update the aria text to match, for example: 'A flowchart of the permission check: root is allowed at once, otherwise a matching owner uid uses the owner bits, then the group bits if the gid is in the group list, then the other bits.'

problem: The example gives chgrp arjun /home/ravi/project/report.txt without saying who runs it. The file's owner is ravi, and Section 2 correctly states that an owner may change the group only to a group the owner belongs to. Ravi is not in arjun, so ravi would get 'Operation not permitted'. Only root can make this change.
fix: Say that the command must be run by root, for example: 'As root: chgrp arjun /home/ravi/project/report.txt. The owner ravi cannot do this himself, because he is not a member of arjun.'

problem: 'No other account has uid 0' is stated as a kernel fact. It is only an administrative convention: a second account created with uid 0 is also the superuser, because the kernel checks the number, not the name.
fix: 'The superuser, root, has uid 0. Any account given uid 0 is also the superuser, so the kernel can test for root with one comparison of the number.'

where: worked example 1, step 7 and the ACL paragraph in Section 3
problem: Adding an ACL entry also sets the ACL mask, which overrides the group permission bits shown in ls -l. Here the mask comes out as r--, so the students do keep read, but the general sentence 'the owner and group stay unchanged, so students keep their access' hides this and will trip students on a file where the mask is smaller than the group bits.
fix: Add one line: 'Adding an entry recalculates the mask, shown in place of the group bits in ls -l. Here the mask is r--, so students keep read; if the mask were smaller, group access would shrink.'
